thought.title: Phoneme /θ/ in “thought”
thought.body: Rest the tip of your tongue lightly between your upper and lower teeth and let air flow softly—avoid releasing a hard /t/ or /s/.

weather.title: Phoneme /ð/ in “weather”
weather.body: Keep the same tongue position as /θ/ while vibrating your vocal cords—avoid hardening it into /d/ or /z/.

through.title: Phoneme /θ/ in “through”
through.body: Keep steady airflow between tongue and teeth before gliding smoothly into a rounded /r/.

theta.tip: Rest the tongue tip lightly between your teeth and exhale softly without a hard /t/ burst.

eth.tip: Use the same tongue placement as /θ/ while vibrating your vocal cords.

r.tip: Curl the tongue tip slightly back without touching the roof of your mouth, lips softly rounded.

ae.tip: Drop your lower jaw wider than /e/ and stretch the corners of your mouth slightly.

ih.tip: Relax your lips and keep the vowel crisp and noticeably shorter than /iː/.

ng.tip: Raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate so air flows through your nose without adding /g/.

sh.tip: Round your lips forward slightly and push a broad, soft stream of air.

ch.tip: Briefly block airflow with the tongue blade, then release crisply through rounded lips.

v.tip: Touch your upper teeth gently to your lower lip and keep voicing even at word endings.

z.tip: Keep your vocal cords vibrating on -s/-es endings after vowels and voiced consonants.

au.tip: Start wide on /a/ and glide smoothly into a rounded /ʊ/.

ei.tip: Glide lightly upward from /e/ toward /ɪ/ at the end of the syllable.

trust.title: Transparent scoring that respects your voice data

voice.title: Your recordings are not stored
voice.desc: LinguaLoop does not keep your audio on its servers. Your voice is only sent to the pronunciation scoring service (Microsoft Azure) and the voice tutor (Google Gemini) to handle that turn.

deterministic.title: Scores you can verify
deterministic.desc: Pronunciation is scored phoneme by phoneme by a dedicated service (Microsoft Azure) and combined with a published formula; word-level dictation results and card intervals use fixed algorithms. The AI chatbot only explains and coaches—it never decides your score.

items.a: Yes. Lessons span A1 through C2, dictation offers 3 difficulty modes (Easy mode only blanks out key words), and starter vocabulary decks let you build momentum in your first 10–15 minutes.

items.q: Which English accent is used for pronunciation scoring?
items.a: Pronunciation scoring uses the 44-phoneme American English standard so target sounds are consistent. When reading sentences or checking the dictionary, you can toggle between US and UK transcriptions anytime.

Free accounts receive one-time trial AI credits to try AI feedback and the tutor. Pro plans grant fresh AI credits every month. Each AI feature has a fixed credit price shown on its button before you use it.

items.q: Do I need to install a mobile app?
items.a: No installation required. LinguaLoop is a responsive web app built for both phone and desktop browsers—you can practice dictation, record shadowing, watch short clips, and review cards anywhere.

items.q: Are my voice recordings saved on the server?
items.a: No. Shadowing clips stay in your browser so you can replay and compare them with the reference audio, and are sent to Microsoft Azure for scoring. When you talk to the voice tutor, audio streams directly to Google Gemini so the tutor can hear and reply, and your browser may use Google's speech recognition to show what you said. LinguaLoop servers keep only scores and word-level results, never audio.
